ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $CD$ bisects the angle between the extensions of sides $AC$ and $BC$, $AD \perp DC$, and point $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$. If $AC=4$ and $BC=6$, what is the length of segment $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $BC$ and $AD$ respectively to meet at point $G$, \\
$\because$ $CD$ bisects the angle between the extended lines of $AC$ and $BC$\\
$\therefore \angle 1=\angle 2$\\
$\because$ $AD\perp DC$\\
$\therefore \angle CDA=\angle CDG=90^\circ$\\
$\because CD=CD$\\
$\therefore \triangle CDG\cong \triangle CDA$ (ASA)\\
$\therefore CG=AC$, $AD=GD$\\
$\because$ $AC=4$, $BC=6$\\
$\therefore BG=BC+CG=6+4=10$\\
Also, $\because$ point $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$\\
$\therefore DE=\frac{1}{2}BG=\boxed{5}$.

method.method_draft: Synthetic extension/congruence route. First read from the image that A, E, B are collinear with E on AB, that C lies on line CB whose extension goes past C, and that AD can be extended to meet the extension of CB at a new point G. From the text use that CD bisects the angle between AC and the extension of BC, and AD is perpendicular to DC. Then in triangles CDA and CDG, the angle at C is equal by the bisector condition, the angle at D is right in both because G lies on the extension of AD, and CD is common; hence triangles CDA and CDG are congruent by ASA. Therefore CG = AC = 4 and DG = AD, so D is the midpoint of AG. Since B, C, G are collinear with C between B and G, BG = BC + CG = 6 + 4 = 10. In triangle ABG, E is the midpoint of AB and D is the midpoint of AG, so DE is a midsegment parallel to BG and DE = BG/2 = 5.

method.method_draft: Analytic reflection/coordinate route. From the image, take CD as the reference axis through C and D, with A on one side of CD and the extension of CB past C on the other side. From the text, since CD bisects the angle between AC and the extension of BC, the reflection of ray CA across line CD lies along the extension of CB. Also AD perpendicular DC means D is the foot from A to the axis CD. Set C as the origin and CD as the x-axis; write A = (p, q), so D = (p, 0) and AC = sqrt(p^2 + q^2) = 4. Reflect A across CD to get G = (p, -q), which lies on the extension of CB and satisfies CG = 4. Since C lies between B and G on the same line and BC = 6, the vector position of B is opposite the direction of G with length 6, so B = -(6/4)G = (-3p/2, 3q/2). The midpoint E of AB is E = ((p - 3p/2)/2, (q + 3q/2)/2) = (-p/4, 5q/4). Then DE has vector E - D = (-5p/4, 5q/4), so DE = (5/4)sqrt(p^2 + q^2) = (5/4)AC = 5.

推理：严格采用坐标反射法。取C为原点，取直线CD为x轴。因为AD⊥DC，所以D是A到x轴的垂足。设A=(p,q)，则D=(p,0)，且AC=sqrt(p^2+q^2)=4。由于CD平分AC与BC延长线之间的角，把点A关于直线CD即x轴反射，得到G=(p,-q)，则G落在BC经过C的延长线上，并且CG=AC=4。又BC=6，且C在B与G之间，所以B与G在同一直线上且方向相反，长度比例为CB:CG=6:4，因此B=-(6/4)G=(-3p/2,3q/2)。E是AB的中点，所以E=((p-3p/2)/2,(q+3q/2)/2)=(-p/4,5q/4)。于是向量DE=E-D=(-p/4-p,5q/4-0)=(-5p/4,5q/4)。因此DE=sqrt(( -5p/4)^2+(5q/4)^2)=(5/4)sqrt(p^2+q^2)=(5/4)AC=(5/4)*4=5。

推理：严格采用坐标反射法。取C为原点，取直线CD为x轴。因为AD⊥DC，所以D是A到x轴的垂足。设A=(p,q)，则D=(p,0)，且AC=sqrt(p^2+q^2)=4。由于CD平分AC与BC延长线之间的角，把点A关于直线CD即x轴反射，得到G=(p,-q)，则G落在BC经过C的延长线上，并且CG=AC=4。又BC=6，且C在B与G之间，所以B与G在同一直线上且方向相反，长度比例为CB:CG=6:4，因此B=-(6/4)G=(-3p/2,3q/2)。E是AB的中点，所以E=((p-3p/2)/2,(q+3q/2)/2)=(-p/4,5q/4)。于是向量DE=E-D=(-p/4-p,5q/4-0)=(-5p/4,5q/4)。因此DE=sqrt(( -5p/4)^2+(5q/4)^2)=(5/4)sqrt(p^2+q^2)=(5/4)AC=(5/4)*4=5。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in quadrilateral $ABCD$, $CD$ bisects the angle between the extensions of sides $AC$ and $BC$, $AD \perp DC$, and point $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$. If $AC=4$ and $BC=6$, what is the length of segment $DE$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Extend $BC$ and $AD$ respectively to meet at point $G$, \\
$\because$ $CD$ bisects the angle between the extended lines of $AC$ and $BC$\\
$\therefore \angle 1=\angle 2$\\
$\because$ $AD\perp DC$\\
$\therefore \angle CDA=\angle CDG=90^\circ$\\
$\because CD=CD$\\
$\therefore \triangle CDG\cong \triangle CDA$ (ASA)\\
$\therefore CG=AC$, $AD=GD$\\
$\because$ $AC=4$, $BC=6$\\
$\therefore BG=BC+CG=6+4=10$\\
Also, $\because$ point $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$\\
$\therefore DE=\frac{1}{2}BG=\boxed{5}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, A, E, B are on the same straight line, and E is located on segment AB; C, B are on the same straight line, and line CB extends toward the outside of C in the direction marked F; D is at the upper left, and segments AD, DC, DE, AC, BC are all drawn. Judging from the position of the figure, if AD is extended and the extension line of line CB outside C is extended, they will intersect at a new point G.

Reasoning: According to the method, construct auxiliary point G, so that the extension of AD intersects the extension of BC at G. The givens state that CD bisects the angle formed by AC and the extension of BC, so ∠ACD = ∠DCG. Also because AD ⟂ DC, and D, A, G are collinear, ∠CDA = ∠CDG = 90°. The two triangles CDA and CDG also have common side CD, therefore △CDA ≅ △CDG (ASA). So CG = AC = 4, and DG = AD, hence D is the midpoint of AG. Since B, C, G are collinear and C is between B and G, BG = BC + CG = 6 + 4 = 10. The givens state that E is the midpoint of AB; in triangle ABG, D is the midpoint of AG and E is the midpoint of AB, so DE is a midline, DE = BG/2 = 5.
